subject: statistics

source.document: Syllabus for examinations in 2028, 2029 and 2030 (0480 Statistics was withdrawn; 0479 is its replacement, first examination 2027)
source.track: IGCSE · ages 14–16 · June series only · all candidates take Paper 1 and Paper 2 (each 50%)

note: Cambridge IGCSE Statistics 0480 was withdrawn, so the program follows its replacement 0479. Units follow the syllabus's twelve numbered subject content sections (1–12) in teaching order; the advanced and expert lessons extend the syllabus's descriptive core into inference, Bayesian thinking and computation.

program.title: Data and its collection
topics: Population, sample, census and representative sample
Sampling methods: simple random, systematic, stratified and quota
Bias in sampling
Selecting samples using a random number table
Open and closed questions in surveys
Classifying data: qualitative, quantitative, discrete and continuous

program.title: Representation of data
topics: Frequency tables and two-way tables
Pictograms, bar charts and pie charts
Venn diagrams
Box-and-whisker diagrams
Stem-and-leaf diagrams
Advantages and disadvantages of different ways of representing data

program.title: Frequency distributions
topics: Ungrouped and grouped frequency distributions
Class limits, boundaries, midpoints and widths
Histograms and frequency density
Frequency polygons
Cumulative frequency distributions, polygons and curves

program.title: Measures of central tendency
topics: Mean, median and mode of small data sets and ungrouped frequency distributions
Estimating the mean and median of grouped data
The modal class
Advantages and disadvantages of each measure and justifying a choice in context

program.title: Quartiles, percentiles and measures of dispersion
topics: Quartiles of small data sets and ungrouped frequency distributions
Estimating quartiles and percentiles of grouped data
Range and interquartile range
Standard deviation
Advantages and disadvantages of each measure and justifying a choice in context

program.title: Transformations of data sets
topics: Effect on the mean and standard deviation of adding a constant or multiplying by a constant
Effect on the median and interquartile range of the same transformations
Effect of introducing or removing values on a statistical measure
Combining two data sets with known means and standard deviations
Standardising data for comparison

program.title: Probability
topics: Probability notation
Calculating probabilities, with and without replacement
Finding the probability of an event not happening
The addition rule
Mutually exclusive and independent events
Conditional probability in simple cases
Tree diagrams for combined events

program.title: Probability distributions
topics: Probability distributions of all possible outcomes
Expectation of a variable from a probability distribution

program.title: Crude and standardised rates
topics: Calculating crude rates of events in a population
The reason for finding a standardised rate
Calculating standardised rates given a standard population
Conclusions from values of crude and standardised rates

program.title: Index numbers
topics: Price relatives for goods and services relative to a base year
The meaning of a price relative
Weighted aggregate index numbers
Interpreting and using a weighted aggregate index number
Limitations of using a weighted aggregate index number

program.title: Bivariate distributions
topics: Independent and dependent variables
Positive, negative, weak, strong and no correlation
Scatter diagrams
Line of best fit by eye and by the method of semi-averages
The equation of a line of best fit
Assumptions when using a line of best fit and the limitations of extrapolation

program.title: Time series
topics: Time series graphs
The reasons for finding moving averages
Calculating and plotting moving averages
Trend and trend lines
Seasonal variation and seasonal components
Predictions from trend lines and their limitations
